So, what, exactly, is going to affect sales effectiveness, marketing precision, and operational efficiencies? All of that. So, these are the predominant data challenges that we see whenever we talk to clients in any industry. Irrespective...
Right? So, typically, we are structured in a way to execute the overall spectrum of all these enterprise data challenges. That is where Dataskate brings enterprise data management strategy.
That's where you see this is a four-step approach. For example, any enterprise data management problems that we need to resolve... It's not exactly important to follow the same series of steps like 1, 2, 3, and 4.
But at the end of the day, for example, one client may talk about... Okay, do you know what I mean? I do have a lot of challenges with my data and siloed systems, all of that. So, that way, we will be fully focused on point number one, which is data quality. We typically try to understand what kind of data quality they do have in their existing systems as of today. For which we have a couple of acclities and dashboards that we have built already.
So, it's a maximum fraction of seconds that we can try to get their file and put it into them, and they will be able to see their data hub quality as bad and moderate data quality issues.
Okay. So, with that being said, we do have data quality services and cloud. That is one thing. The second being... This is the utmost important topic. Typically, whenever clients definitely state the problem, they will talk about, "There are a lot of duplicates in my system." What that clearly tells us is that it is actually a master data problem.
But, in the end, we need to double-click on the master data management topic. It is to be little sense to understand the business problem clearly. If they do have multiple systems entering from multiple authors or maybe multiple data stewards, then while they are distributing the data to the publishing or consuming applications, the same customer is being repeatedly entered multiple ways. Then that's a problem that will definitely hit us in the sales reporting and effectiveness, and everything will definitely become a problem.
So to avoid that, we need to implement the master data management solution. But there is a myth and concept, and typically people say that, "I don't need master data." But we need to evaluate and understand clearly whether that's a real business problem with respect to master data. Then yes, at an enterprise level, we need to educate the client to tell them what the benefit will be
and whether that's really a business case for the master data. The third one being data governance. So typically, for example, let us assume we clearly qualified data. We are sending it after data quality analysis and creating all of those rules and everything. Then how exactly we are governing that data that is through data governance.
So there are multiple tools available in the market. As far as IDMC Informatic we speak, it is called CDGC that's called like cloud data governance and catalog. What it does is there are two ways to basically set up the data governance. Number one, which is a functional where we will basically understand who are the data creators, who are the data owners and who is basically approving the data.
So combination of all of these things, we will have to put together a complete framework where people process and technology comes into play together. So that is the functional setup of governance that we need to establish.
There are multiple ways to implement the data governance like federated governance. Each line of business, they will be having their own data sets to talk about it, right? And they will have their own different standards and everything.
So with that being said, once... Let us assume we set up that particular functional data governance council. Then the second step is to implement the data governance cataloging information where we will bring from multiple sources of information and clients want to understand the entire lineage of that information from where exactly this source it is coming from and how exactly it is being transformed the data.
So end-to-end lineage, cross-linking, and cross-referencing. All of that information will be captured through the metadata, and that's where the cataloging information we'll be able to give it through the data catalog and data governance.
Lastly, which is data privacy and security. As you know, when we basically try to implement any of these three solutions, at the end of the day, how do we really share the data across the bodies? That means, for example, us data, if at all we want to share it to EMA, then they' definitely like GDPR and CCPA, all of these kinds of...
But regulations and most importantly, we need to comply with the regulatory compliances depending on the industry, right? So that is where data privacy and security is the last one. And that is subject to basically look at the business case.
If it is kindly saying only US data, then we may not need to worry about it much. But if they wanted to exchange the data with any of the other countries, then yes, this solution, we might need to basically keep it into our consideration. Let's move on to the next slide. Any questions so far in that first slide?
